plan.estimand: Between-group mean difference in average outcome across 3 repeated measurements
plan.hypothesis: H0: μ_group1 = μ_group2 (no between-group difference); H1: μ_group1 ≠ μ_group2

parameters.name: Marginal standard deviation within each group at each occasion
Number of repeated measurements per participant

assumptions: Multivariate normal observations within each group
Compound symmetry covariance structure across the 3 repeated measurements
Constant correlation 0.5 between all pairs of repeated measures
Constant marginal variance 2.5² = 6.25 at each occasion
No group-by-time interaction
No missing data
Balanced design with equal participants per group
Two-sided hypothesis test at significance level α = 0.05
Between-group comparison via subject-level average (mean of 3 measurements) with pooled t-test (equivalent to between-group F test from repeated-measures ANOVA)
scientific_notes: The analysis collapses the repeated measurements to a single subject-level summary (average across the 3 occasions) and compares the two groups via a two-sample pooled t-test.

Under compound symmetry with correlation ρ = 0.5 and k = 3 repeated measurements, the variance of the subject-level average is: Var(Ȳ_i) = σ²/k × [1 + (k-1)ρ] = 6.25/3 × [1 + 2×0.5] = 6.25/3 × 2 = 4.1667
The standard error of the group mean difference is: SE = √[2 × Var(Ȳ) / n_per_group] = √[2 × 4.1667 / n_per_group]
The noncentrality parameter for a two-sample t-test is: λ = Δ / SE = 2 / √[2 × 4.1667 / n_per_group]
Power is determined by the noncentral t distribution with df = 2n - 2, noncentrality λ, and critical value from the central t distribution at α = 0.05 (two-sided).
